title: Why are basketball hoops 10 feet high?
description: Basketball’s hoop height began with a gym balcony and two peach baskets. Follow the 1891 story, then check what today’s FIBA rules actually measure.

sections.title: A balcony set the starting height
sections.html:
Basketball’s familiar 10-foot hoop height began with a gym balcony. In 1891, James Naismith attached peach baskets to a rail at Springfield College that happened to be ten feet above the floor.

Springfield’s history tells the surprisingly practical story. A feature of one room became part of a worldwide game.

sections.title: Scoring came with a retrieval job
sections.html:
Naismith wanted two boxes for goals. The janitor brought two peach baskets instead, so he fixed one at each end of the balcony.

The bottoms were still in place. A man at each end retrieved the ball after a score and returned it to play. A basket is an excellent container—slightly too good at containing things, in this case.

sections.title: What is the official hoop height now?
sections.html:
FIBA’s 2026 equipment rules put the top edge of each ring at 3,050 mm above the floor: 3.05 metres, approximately ten feet. The rule allows a maximum difference of 6 mm either way.

That height refers to the rim’s upper edge, rather than the bottom of the net or the top of the backboard.

sections.title: A little history above every shot
sections.html:
The original baskets and today’s steel rings look very different. Yet that old balcony measurement is still recognisable in the modern rules.

Next time a hoop looks impossibly high, picture the peach baskets and the person waiting to retrieve the ball. For another memorable sporting measurement, discover why a marathon is 26.2 miles.
